dependency_asset_review: Reviewed the full controller catalog (27 installed distributions, 7897 files, 3232 candidates) plus targeted source inspection. The dedicated test distribution MDAnalysisTests (692 files: raw MD fixtures under data/, engine code, pytest modules) is required verbatim by the analysis's literal import `from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import PSF, DCD, CRD`, so its data cannot be removed. I read the actual test sources (test_rms.py, test_qcprot.py, test_align.py) and greps of the full data/ directory rather than inferring from names. Findings: NO file bundles the exported answers (reviewed 98-frame tables per analysis). adk_oplsaa_CA_rmsf.npy is an RMSF fixture on an unrelated oplsaa trajectory, not any RMSD computation in this notebook. Exact notebook selections are absent from all test code: test_rms.py's `rmsd()` test computes against a different reference (`.calphas` of pre-aligned config in test_rmsd). Contaminating constants (correct_values 4.68953, etc. for select="name CA"; ~4.74920 for all-atom mass-weighted; 4.6997/1.9154/2.7139 for backbone resid 1:10/10:20 groups) differ in select, reference, and ref_frame; none equals any value of the exported CORE-backbone-CA (ref_frame=0 vs same-frame example), resid-weighted (R_charge, resid-1958-and-121), or CORE-as-computed tables. None of these pytest files is executed by the analysis; that they exist as test code rather than answer assets is a fact of the codebase, not something candidates were excluded for. I declare no file removals; these constants are not required inputs (the analysis never opens them), so leaving them installed does not affect the analysis, and removing them would break the MDAnalysisTests package coherently. Also inspected numpy/scipy/pandas/matplotlib candidate lists, which are only heuristically clustered test/example files (pandas/tests..., scipy/stats/tests/test_sensitivity_analysis.py, matplotlib examples) — none related to RMSD analyses or PSF/DCD/CRD data. Remaining uncertainty: only ~10 candidate files were read or hashed line-by-line; the rest were assessed by filenames, greps, or wheel metadata, so this is a targeted, not exhaustive, audit. No evidence of full or partial answer exposure was found in any inspected file.
explanation: All three frozen end-state outputs (core_ca_rmsd.csv = 4134 bytes, mass_weighted_rmsd.csv = 9534 bytes, resid_weighted_rmsd.csv = 9506 bytes) were produced successfully by the controlled offline reference run (exit 0, ~4.4 s, well within the 600 s limit). Environment: Python 3.13.13, MDAnalysis 2.9.0, MDAnalysisTests 2.9.0 (its MDAnalysis/datafiles.py shim is how the literal `from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import PSF, DCD, CRD` import is satisfied). No source adaptations were needed — analysis.py is byte-identical to original.py — because all three input files (adk.psf, adk_dims.dcd, adk_open.crd) ship inside the installed MDAnalysisTests distribution and require no network or cache at run time. Plots work offline via the controller's MPLBACKEND=Agg environment setting. Warnings in the log (SyntaxWarning `\A` in ylabel strings, DCDReader DeprecationWarning, "Shape of C-alpha charges: (214,)") are non-fatal and originate in the untouched source. Offline execution confirmed: the datafiles import resolves to a static path in site-packages (verified `ls` on the data directory shows adk.psf, adk_dims.dcd, adk_open.crd are present in MDAnalysisTests/data), Universe construction requires no network, and no import of MDAnalysisTests triggers any remote fetch — the reference run completed fully offline.
unresolved_assumptions: Reduced-scope asset inspection: I did not open all 7897 installed files individually; the dependency-asset review above is targeted (test_rms.py, test_qcprot.py, test_align.py source reads, full MDAnalysisTests/data/ filename/grep scan, spot hashing of candidate numpy fixtures), not an exhaustive audit of every distribution's test/example files. This is recorded as evidence of specific gaps, not as a claim of blanket absence.

Environment stack pinned to current versions (MDAnalysis 2.9.0, MDAnalysisTests 2.9.0, pandas 3.1.0, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, matplotlib 3.11.2); these work together in my test, but upstream upgrades could in principle change formatting or behavior — not an issue for the frozen offline run I executed.

I did not independently verify scientific fidelity of the notebook's logistics beyond that the exports matched the plan's expected column structure (correct column counts, 98 rows); no external ground-truth RMSD values were available outside the MDAnalysisTests test suite, which I deliberately did not use as a validation oracle.
